question: Should typed transient Slack tool-progress default to thread reaction or suppression when standalone progress is not enabled and no reaction target is available?
rationale: This is an intentional channel-delivery default that can suppress status messages for existing Slack workflows; code review cannot safely choose that user-facing policy without owner intent.

options.title: Adopt typed-progress suppression
options.body: Confirm reaction-or-suppression as the default for explicitly typed transient progress, contingent on current-head agent-path proof.

options.title: Preserve standalone delivery by default
options.body: Keep typed tool-progress as normal Slack posts unless an explicit opt-in enables suppression or reaction.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Limit the change to a documented existing progress mode and defer any broader delivery-default change.

recommendation.title: Adopt typed-progress suppression
recommendation.body: Confirm reaction-or-suppression as the default for explicitly typed transient progress, contingent on current-head agent-path proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person was directly asked to decide the outstanding Slack delivery policy in the PR discussion.
